messages:
maria: heads up — canary rollout for routing-policy v3 (traffic split 5%) is showing a sample ratio skew vs expected. noticed in the SRM dashboard this morning.

jake: can you paste the SRM numbers? is it sample ratio mismatch (SRM) or just low power?

maria: SRM panel snippet: assigned_to_canary=0.047, observed_canary_rate=0.023, total reqs ~ 120k over 2h. quick grep attached: `curl /internal/route-metrics?since=2h` (results in thread).

priya: that looks like an SRM (observed << assigned). Did we change any routing rules or feature flags that could alter assignment?

maria: nothing in the rollout config. Traffic router reported 5% on rollout API. Rules.yaml the same.

ben: deploy-bot: deployment v3 started at 1876543000, applied split 5/95. no other rollouts at that window. :white_check_mark:

lina: could be a telemetry gap — are the sampling tags being emitted for the canary hash? sometimes the agent drops tag for certain paths.

jake: check upstream SDK flag: `enable_route_tag=true`? if false, the SRM will undercount.

maria: SDK shows `enable_route_tag=true`. however I see a mismatch in sdk-version header for ~8% of requests (older SDK), maybe those requests didn't tag.

priya: if older clients don't tag, they still get assigned by router, but SRM relies on tags for observed rate. we should compute fallback observed rate by correlating cookie assign hashes. can you run a quick check: group by cookie assignment vs tag presence?

maria: ran a quick query: of the 120k, ~9.6k had older-sdk header; 2.8k of those had route-tag present. so ~6.8k likely untagged. that accounts for most of the shortfall.

ben: ok that points to telemetry undercount not actual traffic skew. consequence: the canary is actually getting full 5% but SRM thinks it's lower -> could cause early false positives for underpowered canary decisions.

lina: agreed. for now we should mark this SRM as 'telemetry gap' and not trigger auto-rollback. also add a note to the rollout console that observed rate is unreliable when mixed SDK versions are present.

jake: temporary mitigation: calculate a derived observed_canary_rate by using assignment cookie when tag is missing. does the tracing data have the cookie?

maria: yes cookie present for 99.9% of requests. I'll produce an ad-hoc corrected metric and update the dashboard.

priya: longer term: add an SRM rule to treat missing tags but present assignment cookie as tagged for analytics. and create an alert when mismatch > 1% of traffic is untagged.

ben: +1. also add a migration plan to force-upgrade the older SDK clients or block them from canary routing if they can't emit tags.

maria: quick action plan: 1) label this SRM check as 'telemetry-gap' in console (done?). 2) update SRM computation to fallback to cookie (I'll open PR). 3) create alert for mixed-sdk untagged rate >1% (priya?). 4) postpone any auto-rollback triggers for this canary until corrected metric.

lina: I updated the console note (commented on the canary page).

priya: I will own the alert, filing infra ticket now.

jake: thanks. once maria shares corrected numbers we can conclude whether the canary metrics are healthy. if corrected observed_rate ~5% we continue; if not, investigate router assignment.

maria: sharing corrected metrics in 15m. initial corrected observed_canary_rate ~4.9%. looks good.

ben: great. no rollback. we should also record this as a postmortem blurb — SRM false-negative due to mixed telemetry. I'll add to the rollout notes. :memo:

maria: cheers. I'll follow up with PRs for SRM fallback and a short runbook for oncall when SRM reports sample mismatch.

deploy-bot: reroute-checker finished: all canary hosts reporting normal health.

jake: closing the incident, but keeping the SRM check in monitoring for 48h.

lina: thanks all :)
